newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Council concludes on time, leaves others unresolved.
newsitem.headline: Council concludes on time, leaves others unresolved.

text.p: Transport ministers agreed on Tuesday to harmonise the twice-yearly switch to summer time, a defeat for France, but failed to progress much on relations with Switzerland, on lorry taxation or rules on new tachographs.
France failed to persuade its EU counterparts to give it an exemption from the eighth summertime directive, meaning the file should now proceed via the European Parliament to final adoption.

Ministers also agreed to extend to aircraft from 16 developing countries time-limited exemptions from noise rules. For the rest, an agenda cut from two days to one, discussions were largely inconclusive.
Ministers held a discussion on taxing aviation fuels and agreed to pass a draft Dutch resolution to economic and finance ministers.
Dutch Transport & Public Works Minister Annemarie Jorritsma confirmed at a closing news conference that the file would go to ECOFIN, though she could not say when.

Ministers did reach agreement on the terms of reference for future work on Community involvement with the European Organisation for the Safety of Air Navigation (Eurocontrol) and the set-up of a European civil aviation safety body.

Jorritsma failed to persuade ministers to reach political agreement for a common position on a draft regulation amending Regulation 3821/85 and Directive 85/599, which will return to officials before the next attempt at a deal, at the Transport Council in June.

Ministers did agree a resolution on the development of road transport telematics, championed by the Dutch, who wanted a political signal from the Council on common techincal specifications for an electronic fee-collection system.

Jorritsma said ministers also reached political agreement on the proposed regulation to formalise existing aid measures to encourage combined transport operations (Pilot Actions for Combined Transport or PACT).

They reached no final decision, however, on the Commission's "Eurovignette" proposal, having discussed presidency questions on the maximum allowable charge, whether to include differentiation according to trucks' environmental characteristics, the possibilities of lower charges for peripheral countries and the possibility of levying additional charges on Alpine routes, notably the Brenner pass.
Both Kinnock and Jorritsma acknowledged the link between Eurovignette talks and the ongoing EU/Swiss talks on closer road transport relations between the two sides.
No significant progress was apparent on Tuesday although Kinnock said member states had broadly backed the Commission's negotiating stance.
